title: Umqa
author: Mama Nolwazi
desc: Pumpkin cooked to collapse, puréed, then thickened with maize meal and finished with butter — a porridge that eats like a main course and tastes like a dessert.
longDesc: Umqa is what happens when the pumpkin is the liquid. There is no milk and no stock: the pumpkin gives up enough water to cook the maize meal, and what you get is dense, sweet and orange. It goes by isijingi in isiZulu, thophi in Tshivenda and Sepedi, tshopi in Xitsonga and sidvudvu in siSwati — the same idea under six names, which tells you how far back it goes.
steps: Put the cubed pumpkin and the water in a large saucepan over medium heat and cook for about 20 minutes, until the pumpkin is completely soft.
Add the salt and the brown sugar, then blend to a smooth purée with a stick blender.
Return the purée to the pan and whisk the maize meal into it gradually, so it does not go lumpy.
Cook over medium-low heat for 30 to 40 minutes, stirring often with a wooden spoon, until the maize meal has lost its coarseness on the tongue.
Stir in the butter, check the seasoning, and serve warm.
chefTips: The doneness test is texture, not the clock. Taste it: if the maize meal still feels gritty, it needs longer, whatever the timer says.
Whisk the maize meal into the hot purée gradually. Tipped in at once it seizes into lumps that will not break down.
Butterrnut works as well as pumpkin and is easier to peel.
A knob more butter and a spoonful of sugar turns the same pot into breakfast, which is how many households eat it.
commonMistakes: Adding the maize meal all at once, which lumps immediately.
Leaving it unstirred on the low simmer, when it catches on the base of the pan within minutes.
Stopping at thirty minutes because the clock says so, and serving it gritty.
Adding extra water to loosen it. It is meant to be thick enough to hold a spoon upright.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. It sets very firm when cold.
reheating: Reheat gently with a splash of water, stirring until it loosens.
healthBenefits: Pumpkin is rich in beta-carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
A whole kilogram of vegetable in a dish that is usually classed as a starch.
culturalNote: That this dish has a name in at least six South African languages is the point: pumpkin-and-grain porridge is a shared southern African idea rather than one group's invention. Xhosa umqa, Zulu isijingi, Venda and Pedi thophi, Tsonga tshopi and Swazi sidvudvu are the same dish speaking different languages.
